latin: Scitur ex cabala per mysterium partis septentrionalis cur iudicabit deus saeculum per ignem.
translation: It is known from the Kabbalah, through the mystery of the northern part, why God will judge the world through fire.
translation_note: 'partis septentrionalis' (the northern part) is glossed by Farmer's note, shared with the companion thesis 11>45, as the standard kabbalistic association of 'north' and 'fire' with the fifth sefirah, God's judgment or power (paraphrase; farmer1998:27363).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch20, from Latin at farmer1998:27331
attribution: Pico's own opinion (section 11>, Cabalistic conclusions confirming the Christian religion by his own opinion) (farmer1998:27331).
doctrine: Farmer's note, covering theses 11>44-45 together, explains that in medieval Kabbalism 'north' and 'fire' were most often associated with the fifth sefirah, God's judgment or power, and 'water' with the fourth, God's love or piety (paraphrase; farmer1998:27363). Thesis 11>44 uses this association to argue that kabbalistic symbolism accounts for the Christian teaching that God will judge the world by fire (farmer1998:27331).
historiography: A German study of Pico's Kabbalistic epistemology lists thesis 11>44 among a cluster of theses (11>22, 11>44, 11>47) cited together, quoting the Latin of 11>47 in full and citing 11>44 by number alongside it (kabbalah_paradigma:2106); the study's discursive argument, given in German, is not established here.
not_established: The content of the kabbalah_paradigma citation beyond the page and thesis-number reference is not established here, the German text not having been translated (kabbalah_paradigma:2106).
